brief: UBS Prime Services recaps Thursday's US equity sell-off, the largest tech drawdown since Covid, and argues hedge fund (HF) selling was not the driver: HF sells outweighed buys roughly 6x and cut 1.1std of US gross, but this was only the 7th-largest degross day since Oct 1 (vs -2.3std Oct 28, -2.1std Oct 29, -2.2std Oct 21). UBS attributes the move instead to broader AI-beta selling by macro, trend-following systematics and retail, not cutting of favored single-stock longs by equity L/S, which instead ran relative-value trades in Neoclouds and Optical & Networking and made money (Equity L/S +27bps) while quants lost 49bps. Thursday selling concentrated in AI Winners (-1.1std), Crowded Longs (-0.9std) and Hyperscalers (-1.2std); Semis selling was moderate and Memory/Hardware flows were muted despite Memory's -16.6% move, which UBS reads as HFs having already de-risked the AI value chain since summer. Europe flows were net buying, led by dip-buying in Banks and Autos. Japan recorded net selling WTD, which UBS ties to de-risking into the US midterm elections.
